fact_check_log.claim: Instagram: numbers allowed in hashtags; spaces and special characters such as $ or % won't work (as at November 2026, linked)
A hashtag can be added to an already uploaded post by editing the caption or in a comment
You can only tag your own posts, not a guest's photo
A public account's post with a hashtag appears on that hashtag's page
Tapping the tag shows all photos and videos uploaded with it
Posts tagged by private profiles don't appear publicly on hashtag pages (body and FAQ)
eSafety: always ask for consent before sharing a photo or video (linked)
If someone asks you to remove a photo, do it, no questions asked
Consent can be reversed; delete the photo or edit the person out
Once shared online you can lose control of how others use it
People can set accounts to review photos they are tagged in, or stop tagging
Check with other parents before posting, sharing or tagging images of their children (body and FAQ, linked)
Share only with people you know and trust; use privacy settings to limit who sees them
Photos and videos are personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 when identity is clear or reasonably ascertainable (linked)
Privacy Act doesn't apply to photos taken in a personal capacity because it doesn't cover individuals (wording tightened by edit 3)
Posted without permission: ask the poster first, then the site's administrator
